title: Share the header area bootstrap between initHeaderApp and initRepositoryApp
description:
## Summary

https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/264033 added `initRepositoryApp()` and `parseRepositoryAppDataset()`, which copy two pieces of `init_header_app.js`. `initHeaderApp()` still mounts the header on its own for the readme view, so both copies stay after `repository_single_vue_app` is removed. Every new header `inject` or client query then has to be added in two places.

## Proposal

1. **Cache seeding:** export `initClientQueries` from `init_header_app.js` as a util in `~/repository/utils/`, and use it in `init_header_app.js`, `init_repository_page.js` and `init_repository_app.js`. Keep the current guards for empty `projectPath` and `ref`/`escapedRef`.
1. **Header `provide`:** extract the header part of the `provide` into one helper that both `initHeaderApp()` and `parseRepositoryAppDataset()` use. That covers the breadcrumb keys, the `webIdeButtonOptions` destructuring, `downloadLinks`, and the `customCodeDropdownClients` parsing. The `customCodeDropdownClients` parsing is also copied in `pages/projects/show/index.js`.
1. Unit test the helper. `init_header_app.js` has no spec today.

## Related

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/636539: if the dataset becomes one `data-view-model` attribute, do this first, or design the shared helper so it accepts either input.
- Epic: https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/23817
